text.p: Newly-listed Australian insurance and funds management group National Mutual Holdings Ltd on Tuesday posted an 82.6 percent rise in annual profit, beating prospectus forecasts and paying a handsome dividend to giant French parent Axa.
National Mutual said a key factor in its sharp profit increase was a turnaround in the fortunes of its life insurance unit National Mutual Life.

"The profit outcome, together with healthy new business volumes, an 11 percent drop in expenses, and improved investment earnings, reflects a clear emergence of an improvement in the National Mutual Life Group's performance," it said.

The group, which listed in Australia and New Zealand two months ago, said net profit for the year to September 30 nearly doubled to A$210.9 million ($168.7 million) compared with A$115.5 million a year earlier.
National Mutual had forecast a bottom line 1995/96 profit of A$198.0 million in its prospectus.

French insurance group Axa SA, which paid A$1.1 billion for a 51 percent stake last year, will pocket A$34.68 million of the A$68 million in dividends to be paid to shareholders in February next year.
Australian investors welcomed the result, sending National Mutual shares six cents higher to close at A$1.78.
Analysts gave the result cautious approval but said the group's expense levels were far from meeting industry benchmarks.
"They've got a hell of a way to go. It's a slight improvement off a very low base," one Sydney-based analyst said.
It was a fact later acknowledged by National Mutual managing director Geoff Tomlinson.
"We're still not at industry competitive expense rates," Tomlinson told a news conference.
The highlight of the result was a spectacular recovery by National Mutual Life, which achieved a net profit of A$160.5 million in 1995/96 after losing A$26.2 million last year.
Tomlinson was upbeat about the future of the life division.

"In terms of the three things which I look at in a life office, the growth in new business, the retention of (existing) business and the reduction of expenses - everything is trending in the right direction," he said.
National Mutual Asia, which is 56 percent owned by National Mutual Holdings and runs the groups' Hong Kong-based insurance business, contributed A$99.2 million, up 36.3 percent on the previous year.
Tomlinson said the Asian region would continue to be the group's major overseas focus.

"We are working hard to improve our chances of getting a licence to operate in China, an application for entry into Thailand has been made and we have increased our research activity in India, the Philippines and Vietnam," he said.
